proof: Pinned Spring6.1.14 getSynchronizations copies the registered set and sorts with OrderComparator; invokeAfterCompletion iterates that list ascending. Explicit MIN precedes production MAX, without reliance on a tie. Primary tagged OrderComparator uses List.sort; same-order sorting is stable, but this observer pair has distinct orders.
registration: after original super.prepareSynchronization once; expected owner created only in actual STATUS_COMMITTED afterCompletion, before later production callback schedules real stop. ROLLED_BACK/UNKNOWN register nothing. No prospective beforeCommit registration.
stickyFailure: Spring catches/logs callback Throwables and continues, so observer catches/stores a sticky failure itself; source main and cleanup inspect it. It cannot silently pass or stand in for successful registration.
